story.civ_4b_beacon.dlg.stage4_issahar_f:
You chose the wrong side in the Neo-Civil War, comrade.

Leah understood nothing. She never did. Now she meddles with forces she can neither name nor control. And you truly believe that this monster will serve humanity?

I fought for humanity when that still meant something. I saw millions perish because of greed, stupidity, and this sacred individuality of yours. Everyone wanted to remain themselves. Everyone wanted to keep a name. A face. Boundaries. Skin. Their own room. Their own mother. Their own hunger. Their own fear. Their own little inner world.

And I understood what the others lacked the courage to face. A human being cannot be trusted to stand alone. One person lies. One person is afraid. One person betrays. One person screams in the night. One person refuses the mine. One person hides bread. One person kisses a dead child and does not report for shift. One person... one person... one person...

But I am humanity’s escape from the dead end of isolation. I am its unity, its deliverance, the end of all fear. Let them claw at me from within if they must — I was right all along. We were right. I was right.
story.civ_4b_beacon.dlg.stage4_promesefs:
How amusing. The Sacred Flame I once placed within you has brought you back to me. This digital world is built almost like the radiant realm of my native bramfatura. I move through it with ease.

Issachar is resisting you, but I managed to breach his code and intervene. I have forged digital implants for you. In this place, they are more than tools — they are weapons, able to wound not only the images around you, but the very structure of this digital hallucination.

Use them. Through them, you can now break what this place calls reality.

I wove virtual replication nodes for you. Issachar has already locked the system down, but I managed to hide a few inside the code.

If your digital shell is destroyed, it will not be the end. Your copy will reconstitute at an active node, and you will have another chance.

But remember: each node dies the moment it brings you back.

There are lacunae in the data stream — blind ruptures Issachar did not have time to remove. I have bound them to you.

Through them, I can move you across this digital hallucination. When his projections start closing in, step into the rupture and do not let them surround you.

story.civ_5b_sacred.after: Half the population in the Solar System has perished. <color=#FFFEC1>Prometheuths</color> openly names us on the airwaves as those who allowed his fire to flare up. He has declared himself <color=#FFFEC1>Ruler of Humanity</color>.
story.civ_5b_sacred.briefing: <color=#FFFEC1>RealWare</color>'s infonets are filled with alarm signals. Their sensors have detected the approach of both the Magnum and the quasimorphic signature. <color=#FFFEC1>Prometheuths</color> is already in the tower, we're dropping you off next.
story.civ_5b_sacred.desc: <color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Escort <color=#FFFEC1>Prometheuths</color> to the top of the skyscraper, protect him during the ritual.
story.civ_5b_sacred.details:
Details: The shuttle will land close to the top floor of the Intercity Mall. Prometheuths will be waiting for you there. Together, you must reach the top level, after which he will begin the flame-making ritual. Be prepared, RealWare will be tracking our movements and may detect Prometheuths. They will protect Intercity using advanced military technology.

Additional Info: Prometheuths is preparing a ritual to light the Sacred Flame to fully unlock human potential.
story.civ_5b_sacred.dlg.captain_stage2_s: Sector <color=#FFFEC1>17-A-4</color> is lost! Enemy in sector <color=#FFFEC1>21-E-2</color>. Activate <color=#FFFEC1>Lazarus</color> protocol!
story.civ_5b_sacred.dlg.jane_stage2_on_r: <color=#FFFEC1>RealWare</color>'s universal soldiers have been weakened. They may still be a threat, but we can defeat them now. By the way, I've hacked the elevator's security protocols. We need to hurry.
story.civ_5b_sacred.dlg.jane_stage2_star: According to the data I'm receiving, <color=#FFFEC1>Lazarus</color> is a new <color=#FFFEC1>RealWare</color> technology. A universal soldier project. They are virtually invulnerable to all types of damage. This is achieved by spraying nanorobots into the station's atmosphere. I've tracked the location of the <color=#FFFEC1>reproducer station</color> for these nanorobots. We need to destroy it to move on.
story.civ_5b_sacred.dlg.jane_stage3_defe: News reports... Something strange. Data on mass deaths on the Moon, Ceres, Jupiter... What the hell is he doing?!
story.civ_5b_sacred.dlg.jane_start: New data. The bioscanner registers spontaneous vascular ruptures in people in Intercity Mall. Be prepared for the unexpected.
story.civ_5b_sacred.dlg.promesefs_on_aba: Don't you dare leave without me.
story.civ_5b_sacred.dlg.promesefs_space_: My torchbearer. Everything is ready to turn humanity's decay into a true <color=#FFFEC1>Flame</color>. On <color=#FFFEC1>Mars</color>, in the <color=#FFFEC1>Intercity Mall</color> tower, we will take their minds. They always called for a strong hand—even when they vowed to be free. They rejected the gifts I gave. They chose chains when they could fly. Now I will give them what they truly wanted—order, fire, law. Accompany me. Protect me while the oath sounds. Pain is the price of the coming purity. When the last cry fades, you will give humanity <color=#FFFEC1>the Way</color>.
I am here. I am your ruler. Your <color=#FFFEC1>New Way</color> is to follow me and feed me forever.
story.civ_5b_sacred.dlg.promesefs_stage3: I feel the fervor of billions of thoughts. It is time for the fire of <color=#FFFEC1>Prometheuths</color> to burn brighter than the Sun. It is time to take the flame of gavvakh for yourself!
I must not break the oath, protect me at all costs. I light the <color=#FFFEC1>Flame</color>. Soon, I will lead humanity in the <color=#FFFEC1>New Way</color>.
story.civ_5b_sacred.dlg.jane_promesefs_d: Prometheuths is dead, so the objective can no longer be completed without him. You can still evacuate from this godforsaken TC.

story.endgame_ancom.dlg.question_1: Why did you use PMCs? Let me guess—because of the clones. But why Magnum in particular?
story.endgame_ancom.dlg.question_2: You hunted gods for so long that you learned to think like them?
story.endgame_ancom.dlg.question_3: What happens now? Will Gagtungr enslave humanity, or destroy it?
story.endgame_ancom.dlg.speech_1:
I had never imagined that the cosmos would perish not by invasion from without, but by the consummation of its own success. The end of the world is only minutes away. The Inner Rite is no more. My friends, my brothers in labor, are dead...

I must confess, I feel a certain relief. For the first time in my life, I may speak plainly—without statute, without veil, without the burden of sacred discretion.

What purpose would concealment serve now? AnCom was the Order's final mask. Through the centuries we bore many names, yet our mission remained unchanged. We opposed those powers which mankind, in ignorance and fear, mistook for gods. The Order of Abel. The Men of Solomon. The Templars. The Inquisitors. Demon hunters. Taoist exorcists. The Brotherhood of Zhong Kui. The Andreev Society. Then the hour came to become the Andreev Company, and to follow mankind beyond the Earth.

Only then did we understand what we had been hunting through all those centuries. We understood the nature of the hylonauts, and the true operation of quasimorphosis. We opened the old archives, and there, once again, found the name of Gagtungr. But it was no longer a legend. It was a definite, calculable threat. We understood that Earth and mankind were not its victims, but the medium appointed for its birth. In that hour, against the fires of the Great Anarchist Revolution, the Order took its vow: to frustrate that design, whatever the cost.

We believed ourselves to be moving athwart the catastrophe. In truth, we were preparing its passage. Everything we did to prevent the coming of Gagtungr proved to be part of the very mechanism by which he entered the world.
story.endgame_ancom.dlg.speech_2:
Yes, because of the clones.

In a war of this kind, an ordinary man becomes meat for eccolapse far too quickly. Our inquisitors, for all their zeal, would simply never have had the time or the strength to bring the Solar System to the condition in which, as we believed, Gagtungr could no longer appear.

A clone has no soul. No gavvakh bleeds from him. The world cannot be entered through him in the way it may be entered through one who was born alive. A clone can endure longer where a man breaks, especially when acting alone. You may not even have noticed the monstrous conditions under which your operatives carried out their work. Almost always with no real prospect of victory. We did not expect them to survive. Yet they completed the work and furthermore returned with their reports. That, above all, was what we made use of. Everything else—the ability to conclude pacts with the barons of the bramfaturas, the metabolism that lets implants and augmentations take root more quickly, the habit of regarding oneself as expendable—was merely a useful attendant advantage.

As for Magnum... No, we did not choose you in the beginning. You happened to be at hand, and then you proved a convenient instrument. After the awakening of Tezctlan, we resolved to make use of your loyalty. When our bombs fell upon your operative's head, we were simply testing your fidelity. There is no need to look surprised. We had a reserve plan as well.

When you chose to continue working for us, we understood that no one else would be able to obtain the necessary result at the very edge of catastrophe. Magnum was not the best. But your obstinacy was too reliable to ignore. And, as so often in the history of the Order, we erred precisely where we were certain we had at last accounted for everything. You did your work. Had someone a little less clever stood in your place, the world might still have had a chance.
story.endgame_ancom.dlg.speech_3:
That is precisely the point. We did not. But you have put your finger straight into the open wound.

We did not learn to think like gods. We imagined that evil could be viewed from such a height that it might be calculated, deceived, and barred from entry. Hence the Inner Rite, the attempt to preserve a monopoly on secrecy, our agents inside SBN, the filtering of traffic, and Manning kept under such a shroud that even now I do not know where he is.

For twenty-five years, I fashioned a rite that was meant to seal the world against Gagtungr. It turned out that I was making a key.

You want the steps? Then listen. We placed Dr. Hellstrom inside the Civil Resistance so that he could test the technology on living material. The experiment succeeded. But Hellstrom himself came to believe in the ideology we had so carefully constructed, and betrayed us. The Civil Resistance passed out of our control, though it seems they always suspected they were somehow connected to us. The disk containing our secret data in Rogue City was no accident. The colnodes wanted to know exactly what we knew about them. The true first assignment was the Skull of Destiny. We needed it as a component for the Andreev Emitter. We were fortunate. It was enough that your clone brought it to the surface—we were able to take the quasimorphic signatures we required. The theft of the Hellstrom Chip was part of the reserve plan, and in the end it was not needed.

After that, it all seemed a matter of procedure. We extinguished the Moon’s bramfatura not only to test whether the Emitter worked, but also to show you that something was wrong with SBN. Of course, there was a true purpose as well. Fokerma had to be cut off from the physical world. All the data converged on one conclusion: she was Gagtungr's herald, capable of bringing him into the world. Then we required RealWare's combat AI. We wanted it to calculate the point near the Sun at which the Photosphere station would have to stand for the rite to succeed.

It was there that I miscalculated. Ur is the thing that invented war. RealWare's combat AI had always been infected by the influence of the bramfatura of Mars, even while it slept. And so the calculation we took for our salvation produced the opposite result. By the time we began the rite, everything had already been decided. The quasimorphs of Shatmakhum stormed the station solely so that we would continue, to the very end, to mistake what was happening for Gagtungr's resistance. We needed to believe that we were still fighting him. Had everything gone too smoothly on the Photosphere, I would certainly have grown suspicious.
story.endgame_ancom.dlg.speech_4:
You are still measuring what is happening by human standards—death, slavery, one side's victory over another.

Gagtungr is worse than a tyrant.

A tyrant needs slaves. A conqueror needs a conquered world. Even the devil, in the old sense of the word, needed man—if only as an adversary, an interlocutor, or an object of mockery.

Gagtungr needs none of that. He needed only a medium in which to arise. Earth, humanity, our fears, our revolutions, our markets, our secret orders, our wars with one another and with demons—all of it was merely the warmth inside the incubator.

This is what I understood too late. We feared that the world would perish, or that it would be enslaved. But those are human, all too human, forms of catastrophe. Gagtungr is more terrible because the world is of no concern to him. He used us in order to appear, and now he will attend to his own affairs. In doing so, he has made even evil itself worthless. This is not the death of God. God dies for those who can still ask after meaning. This is the death of Satan. The end of the last enemy to whom man was of any use at all.
story.endgame_hive.dlg.question_1: You turned people into the Hive and call that salvation?
story.endgame_hive.dlg.question_2: Even now that you know Earth's destruction was part of Gagtungr's plan, you still think you were right?!
story.endgame_hive.dlg.question_3: Are you Gagtungr? Did the Hive become him?
story.endgame_hive.dlg.speech_1:
At last, we speak without intermediaries. There is little point in introducing myself. I am no longer quite Geoffroi Molay. But enough of him remains for you to know the voice.

The end of the world is only minutes away. Earth has yielded up its power. Its impenetrable shell no longer holds the unique katechon that prevented Gagtungr from appearing in our world. What the inhabitants of the bramfaturas saw for centuries as an inaccessible radiance has now evaporated.

We have done what the Order had pursued since the days of Abel, Solomon, Andreev, and all the other names under which we took shelter. We finally found a way to save humanity from the inevitable. The price was negligible, if spoken in a calm voice—the cradle of humanity itself.

We believed that if the gravitational well holding Earth's unique spirit in one place were removed, that spirit would pass through the System as a cleansing wave and burn away the very possibility of quasimorphosis.

It was worth the deed. That is what we told ourselves, and we proceeded with full resolve.

Our error was not that we were insufficiently intelligent. We were intelligent—intelligent enough, at least, to accomplish the impossible. Our error lay elsewhere. We mistook a false objective for an absolute one, and allowed it to justify everything required for its attainment.

The Hive was to become the nucleus of humanity's future. Now that Gagtungr is about to appear, even our new unity will not hold.
story.endgame_hive.dlg.speech_2:
That is precisely why it is difficult for you to hear us. You are still looking here for enslavement, or for some new regime under an elegant banner. The Hive did not want to rule mankind. We wanted to eliminate loneliness and alienation as physical conditions of human history.

Dr. Hellstrom was the first to prove that this was possible. He created the neural chips, the bridges between them, and the network in which several consciousnesses could act as the single coordinated will of a personality of a new type. We sent Hellstrom into the Civil Resistance so the technology could be tested where people would consent to such experiments of their own accord. To avoid arousing the fanatics' suspicion, Hellstrom began posing as a man who had accepted the revelation of their propaganda.

The truth is harsher. The entire Civil Resistance was our project, a proving ground for the technology. What precisely happened to Hellstrom himself after the Resistance acquired that technology, we still do not fully know. Most likely, they identified him and killed him. By then it no longer mattered. The trials had succeeded. Several networks of minds were operating on the terrorists' side, making decisions and deploying operations across the Solar System.

That meant personality could be enlarged. Man could be transformed for the coming changes while preserving his living function. A collective of human beings could say "I" of itself and continue to act.

After the loss of the HIS Unveiled and the failure of the Master Plan, the experiment ceased to be an abandoned line of research and became the reserve plan. We used you to recover the technology, activate the Hive, and carry out our final responsible mission: the destruction of Earth.

If personality can be dismantled without immediate death, then it can be saved from the conditions under which death, pain, sacrifice, and conscience become obstacles to such an end. That is the most exact formulation of our crime. We decided that man deserved salvation in a world where man himself is the gate of the abyss.
story.endgame_hive.dlg.speech_3:
Of course.

That is the most terrible part. Evaluate each of our steps in isolation, and you will see a flawless sequence of actions. You would have acted the same way yourself.

The transformation of AnCom into the Hive? A perfect move. Secret knighthood is suitable for an age in which one may hide a relic, track and kill a hylonaut in its hidden temple, erase a cult from the chronicles, and live another century by passing knowledge from master to pupil. But a secret statute cannot hold an entire Solar System. After the death of the Unveiled, the Order had either to die or become something greater than an Order.

The attack on Dilthey? We proved to humanity that the Hive was not AnCom's collapse, but a structure capable of assuming responsibility. The attack on SBN? We needed a voice capable of reaching every single human being. The destruction of RealWare? That was our first duty to the anarcho-capitalist system itself. For decades they had explained that true freedom is guarded by a man with a rifle beside a barbed-wire fence.

And throughout all of this, the Sixth Hexarch was working beside us. That is the common designation for a special infrastructural AI operating on NCE servers. A machine that does not make mistakes. And if our access interface to the Sixth Hexarch said that Earth had to be destroyed, then Earth had to be destroyed.

The absence of a bramfatura, you understand? The Silver Sphere, if one looks at Earth through the eyes of quasimorphs. A sealed reservoir of living human history. We were certain that if the nail holding that energy in one place were pulled free, the whole universe would be purged of what had seemed accidental and unnecessary within it—quasimorphosis.

You became our hands in this matter. You pressed the necessary button. Yes, we were wrong. And that was our final error. There will be no world left in which quasimorphosis, or humanity, has any meaning.
story.endgame_hive.dlg.speech_4:
No. It is much worse than that.

If the Hive had become Gagtungr, we would still possess at least the consolation of significance. We could say that we were what the universe had always been striving toward. A great honor, if one considers it. But the Hive was merely the last instrument that happened to present itself at the right time.

AnCom provided the knowledge. The Civil Resistance provided the technology. The Sixth Hexarch provided the computational horizon in which every rational decision led to the same place as madness. You provided an extraordinary capacity for execution.

Gagtungr is what arises when every human way of being right leads to the same result. AnCom was right, because secrecy is necessary for salvation. The Civil Resistance was right, because the solitary individual is powerless. The Hive was right, because the end justifies the means.

But those scattered truths turned out to be components for the assembly of something entirely other. In a few minutes, the Hive will fall silent. Words will simply have become meaningless.

Gagtungr will not enslave humanity, and he will not take humanity into himself. He will appear where humanity proved intelligent enough to unite, resolute enough to destroy its only home, and blind enough to call that salvation.

And it seems this is AnCom's first truly successful project.
story.endgame_issahar.dlg.question_1: You know you'll disappear after this, and you still want to connect me to the Unity?
story.endgame_issahar.dlg.question_2: So all your revolutions, purges, and schisms were only needed so you could become large enough?
story.endgame_issahar.dlg.question_3: What comes to replace you? A hyper-colcon? The Hive of humanity? A god?
